## README.md

### WireLint

[![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/felipefoz/wire-lint/ci.yml?branch=main&label=CI)](https://github.com/felipefoz/wire-lint/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
![Language: Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/language-Rust-orange)
![Status: Beta](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-beta-yellow)
![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20Linux-blue)
![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)

![WireLint: LabVIEW static analysis](docs/assets/wirelint-hero.svg)

Static Analysis for LabVIEW.

WireLint aims to provide an independent static-analysis tool for LabVIEW files, similar in purpose to NI's VI Analyzer. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by National Instruments (NI). LabVIEW is a trademark of NI.

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development setup and contribution guidelines.

WireLint is licensed under the MIT License. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

#### Documentation

- [LLM project overview](llms.txt)
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)
- [Install from GitHub Releases](docs/user-guide/installation.md)
- [Getting started and CLI usage](docs/user-guide/cli.md)
- [Rule configuration](docs/user-guide/configuration.md)
- [Quality and hygiene rules](docs/user-guide/quality-rules.md)
- [Security analysis rules](docs/user-guide/sast-rules.md)
- [GitLab and GitHub code quality reports](docs/user-guide/ci-reports.md)
- [Configuration template](docs/wirelint.example.yaml)
- [Project roadmap](docs/roadmap.md)

#### Security analysis

Run `wirelint security <folder>` to find credentials stored in VI string defaults,
such as default values of password controls or embedded tokens. See the
[security rules](docs/user-guide/sast-rules.md) and the security section in the
[shared configuration template](docs/wirelint.example.yaml).

---

## src\analysis.rs

### Finding

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Finding {
    pub path: PathBuf,
    pub rule: &'static str,
    pub severity: Severity,
    pub message: String,
}
```

A rule violation associated with one scan-relative file path.

### AnalysisError

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct AnalysisError {
    pub path: PathBuf,
    pub message: String,
}
```

A file that could not be analyzed; never represented as a passing check.

### Skipped

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Skipped {
    pub path: PathBuf,
    pub rule: &'static str,
    pub object: Option<formats::ObjectId>,
}
```

An enabled rule suppressed by a directive in the same file.

### Report

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct Report {
    pub analyzed: usize,
    pub findings: Vec<Finding>,
    pub errors: Vec<AnalysisError>,
    pub skipped: Vec<Skipped>,
}
```

Findings and errors accumulated in discovery/registry order.

### impl Report

```rust
impl Report {
    pub fn exit_status(&self, fail_on: FailOn) -> u8;
}
```


### analyze

```rust
pub fn analyze(root: &Path, files: &[PathBuf], config: &Config, category: RuleCategory, rules: &[&dyn Trait]) -> Report
```

Reads each file once and runs every enabled rule over the extracted facts.

File errors are recorded and scanning continues. When all rules are disabled,
discovered files are not read and the analyzed count is zero. `rules` is
the active registry for the selected command.

## src\config.rs

### FailOn

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Deserialize, Serialize, PartialEq, ValueEnum)]
pub enum FailOn {
    Error,
    Warning,
    None,
}
```

Findings at or above this level cause exit status 1; analysis errors always fail.

### impl FailOn

```rust
impl FailOn {
    pub fn exceeded_by(self, severity: Severity) -> bool;
}
```


### DebuggingState

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Deserialize, Serialize, PartialEq)]
pub enum DebuggingState {
    Enabled,
    Disabled,
}
```

Debugging state that produces a finding, independent of rule enablement.

### TerminalDisplayStyle

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Deserialize, Serialize, PartialEq)]
pub enum TerminalDisplayStyle {
    DataType,
    Icon,
}
```

Preferred front-panel terminal display style, independent of rule enablement.

### PathTarget

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Deserialize, Serialize, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum PathTarget {
    Windows,
    Linux,
}
```

Filesystem syntax checked by the path-usage rule.

### DEFAULT_PATH_TARGETS

```rust
pub const DEFAULT_PATH_TARGETS: [PathTarget; N]
```

Platforms checked when the path rule has no explicit targets.

### RuleConfig

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
pub struct RuleConfig {
    pub enabled: bool,
    pub severity: Option<Severity>,
    pub minimum_version: Option<Version>,
    pub maximum_version: Option<Version>,
    pub fail_when: Option<DebuggingState>,
    pub preferred_style: Option<TerminalDisplayStyle>,
    pub allowed_patterns: Option<Vec<String>>,
    pub targets: Option<Vec<PathTarget>>,
}
```

Common options and validated options for individual built-in rules.

### saved_version_bounds

```rust
pub fn saved_version_bounds(options: Option<&RuleConfig>) -> (Option<Version>, Option<Version>)
```

Resolves saved-version bounds, including the maximum-only exception.

### RuleCategory

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum RuleCategory {
    Lint,
    Security,
}
```

Selects which rule section supplies overrides for a command.

### Config

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
pub struct Config {
    pub fail_on: FailOn,
    pub exclude_folders: Vec<String>,
}
```

Versioned configuration with all built-ins enabled unless overridden.

## src\formats\heap\graph.rs

### DiagramGraph

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct DiagramGraph {
    pub objects: BTreeMap<i32, GraphObject>,
    pub signals: BTreeMap<i32, Signal>,
    pub issues: Vec<GraphIssue>,
}
```

Saved object definitions and wire nets, with unresolved topology kept visible.

### GraphObject

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct GraphObject {
    pub class: i32,
    pub parent: Option<i32>,
    pub flags: Option<u32>,
    pub dco: Option<i32>,
    pub primitive_id: Option<i32>,
    pub call_slot: Option<i32>,
    pub primitive_slot: Option<i32>,
    pub constant_value: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    pub constant_display: Option<i32>,
    pub ambiguous_constant_display: bool,
}
```

One heap object; numeric identities and flags have no inferred semantics.

### Signal

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Signal {
    pub diagram: i32,
    pub terminals: Vec<i32>,
    pub state: Option<i32>,
}
```

A saved signal is a net with any number of endpoints, not a pairwise edge.

### GraphIssue

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum GraphIssue {
    TooFewEndpoints { signal: i32 },
    UnresolvedTerminal { signal: i32, terminal: i32 },
    NonTerminalEndpoint { signal: i32, object: i32 },
    CrossDiagramEndpoint { signal: i32, terminal: i32 },
    DuplicateEndpoint { signal: i32, terminal: i32 },
    SharedTerminal { terminal: i32, first: i32, second: i32 },
}
```

Evidence that prevents interpreting a saved net as fully resolved topology.

### impl DiagramGraph

```rust
impl DiagramGraph {
}
```

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Ord, PartialOrd)]
```

A source object's identity; names and coordinates are not identifiers.

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Directive {

}
```

Exact directive text with a resolved arrow target, or a file-wide scope.

### read_directives

```rust
pub fn read_directives(path: &Path, bytes: &[u8], bookmarks: Vec<Vec<u8>>) -> io::Result<Vec<Directive>>
```

Resolves VI comment arrows; XML description directives remain file-wide.

Invalid or ambiguous saved references return an analysis error, never a
file-wide fallback. Unlinked front-panel labels do not supply directives.

### read_diagram_graph

```rust
pub fn read_diagram_graph(bytes: &[u8]) -> io::Result<Option<heap::graph::DiagramGraph>>
```

Extracts saved diagram topology on demand, without launching LabVIEW.

Missing source is `None`; unresolved connections are graph issues, not proof
of safety. This foundation does not resolve callees or perform taint analysis.

### CallEvidence

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct CallEvidence {
    pub calls: Vec<i32>,
    pub incomplete: Vec<(i32, String)>,
}
```

Generic per-rule call evidence and unresolved input paths.

### Version

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, Ord, PartialEq, PartialOrd)]
pub struct Version {
    pub major: u8,
    pub minor: u8,
}
```

LabVIEW major and minor release numbers, ordered numerically.

### impl Version

```rust
impl Version {

```

### FileFacts

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct FileFacts {
    pub path_values: Option<Vec<PathValue>>,
    pub call_inputs: std::collections::BTreeMap<&'static str, CallEvidence>,
    pub separate_compiled_code: bool,
    pub has_description: Option<bool>,
    pub saved_version: Option<Version>,
    pub debugging_enabled: Option<bool>,
    pub has_breakpoints: Option<bool>,
    pub auto_error_handling: Option<bool>,
    pub has_password: Option<bool>,
    pub linked_library: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub library_members: Option<Vec<String>>,
    pub orphaned_vi: Option<bool>,
    pub has_mutation_history: Option<bool>,
    pub terminal_icon_styles: Option<Vec<bool>>,
    pub connector_pane_pattern: Option<u8>,
    pub default_string_values: Option<Vec<DefaultStringValue>>,
    pub diagram_string_values: Option<Vec<DiagramStringConstant>>,
}
```

Facts shared by all rules; extracted once for each analyzed file.

### read_path_values

```rust
pub fn read_path_values(path: &Path, bytes: &[u8]) -> io::Result<Option<Vec<PathValue>>>
```

Reads path values from VI source heaps without using the host filesystem.

### read_facts

```rust
pub fn read_facts(path: &Path, bytes: &[u8], read_version: bool, read_description: bool, read_password: bool) -> io::Result<FileFacts>
```

Reads a VI-family RSRC file or an XML project/library/class document.

Missing XML source-only or description properties mean false. When
`read_version` is true, missing or malformed version metadata is an error.
When `read_password` is true, malformed BDPW metadata is an error.
XML owner descriptions are always validated to extract suppression directives.
Malformed documents and unsupported binary layouts return `InvalidData`,
never an assumed value.

### read_facts_with_orphaned_vi

```rust
pub fn read_facts_with_orphaned_vi(path: &Path, bytes: &[u8], read_version: bool, read_description: bool, read_password: bool, read_orphaned_vi: bool, read_connector_pane_pattern: bool, read_default_strings: bool) -> io::Result<(FileFacts, Vec<Vec<u8>>)>
```

Reads facts and suppression directives, optionally extracting library links.

### directive_rule

```rust
pub fn directive_rule(text: &[u8]) -> Option<&[u8]>
```

Extracts the rule ID from an exact, case-sensitive two-token directive.

The `#` must be the first byte. Only ASCII whitespace separates tokens.

## src\reports.rs

### Format

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, ValueEnum)]
pub enum Format {
    Gitlab,
    GitlabSast,
    Sarif,
}
```

Supported machine reports; destinations are selected separately by the CLI.

### ScanTimes

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct ScanTimes {
    pub started_at: SystemTime,
    pub finished_at: SystemTime,
}
```

Wall-clock bounds for one completed analysis pass.

### render

```rust
pub fn render(report: &Report, format: Format, rules: &[&dyn Trait], times: ScanTimes) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>>
```

Serializes a complete report as UTF-8 JSON without a BOM.

Paths remain relative to the scan root. Rejects non-UTF-8 paths rather than
emitting ambiguous lossy names. Analysis errors are SARIF invocation failures
and GitLab SAST scan messages, not rule findings; GitLab Code Quality
consumers must also check the process exit status.
`rules` is the registry that produced `report`; SARIF lists its full rule
metadata, including any CWE tags, independent of which rules produced findings.

### CONNECTOR_PANE_PATTERNS

```rust
pub static CONNECTOR_PANE_PATTERNS: [(&str, u8); N]
```

Name and terminal count of each of LabVIEW's 36 fixed connector pane
patterns, indexed by the pattern's catalog offset (its raw `pattern`
field, from the VI's own Function TypeDesc, right-shifted by 3).

## src\rules.rs

### Severity

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Deserialize, Serialize, Eq, Ord, PartialEq, PartialOrd)]
pub enum Severity {
    Info,
    Warning,
    Error,
}
```

Ordered finding severity, independent of the configured failure threshold.

### impl fmt::Display for Severity

```rust
impl fmt::Display for Severity {
}
```


### Rule

```rust
pub trait Rule: Sync {
    fn id(&self) -> &'static str;
    fn description(&self) -> &'static str;
    fn default_severity(&self) -> Severity;
    fn supports_call_suppression(&self) -> bool;
    fn check(&self, facts: &FileFacts, options: Option<&RuleConfig>) -> Option<String>;
    fn cwe(&self) -> &'static [&'static str];
}
```

Stateless analysis of facts extracted once by the format layer.

Rules do not read files, print output, or decide process exit status.


## src\scan.rs

### discover_files

```rust
pub fn discover_files(root: &Path, exclude_folders: &[String]) -> io::Result<Vec<PathBuf>>
```

Finds supported LabVIEW file candidates under `root`.

Traversal is recursive, skips symbolic links and excluded child directories,
and returns paths relative to `root` in sorted order. Exclusions match literal
folder names case-sensitively at every depth; the root itself is never excluded.

#### Errors

Returns an error if `root` is not a directory or any filesystem operation
fails during traversal.
